thread:
marta: Heads up — getting intermittent 502s from inference pods in eu-west-1 when traffic goes through edge-lb-eu-b :confused:
kevin: saw that too earlier, only from requests originating in AZ-b, AZ-a is fine :thinking_face:
alyssa: any recent node drains or spot reclaim in that AZ? could be sticky conntrack to drained IPs
deploy-bot: autoscaler: initiated drain of spot-gpu-23 (eu-west-1b) for Spot interruption at 2256788600 UTC :bell:
kevin: ok that matches timing. but why only AZ-b? endpoint slices should update quickly
sara: copying `kubectl get endpointslice -n inference -l service=infer-gpu -o wide` output i pulled right after the drain:
```
NAME                          ADDRESSTYPE   PORTS   ENDPOINTS
infer-gpu-azb-2               IPv4          8000    10.2.5.8,10.2.5.9
infer-gpu-aza-1               IPv4          8000    10.1.3.7
```
kevin: weird — endpointslice for AZ-b still had the drained IP before controller reconciled. but we usually see fast propagation
alyssa: what kube-proxy mode? ipvs or iptables? ipvs can maintain sticky connections if endpoints flip
kevin: ipvs on these clusters. conntrack dump shows entries pointing to 10.2.5.8:8000 with state ESTABLISHED even after node drained
marta: so healthchecks from the internal LB hit the kube-proxy IPVS entry which routes to stale pod ip -> gots a TCP RST because pod gone -> 502 to client
sara: also noticed node-local-dns TTL was set to 60s in the configmap, but stub resolver caching on edge nodes is longer (120s). possible split where DNS points to headless svc IP that maps to endpointslice not yet reconciled
kevin: summary hypothesis: spot drain -> endpointslice partial propagation in AZ-b + ipvs sticky/conntrack entries -> LB healthchecks continue to route to dead pod IP -> 502s. DNS TTL mismatch makes some callers still prefer old AZ routing
alyssa: actionable checklist:
- force endpointslice resync for infer-gpu
- clear conntrack entries on edge LB and node-proxy in AZ-b (careful, will drop in-flight)
- align node-local-dns and cluster DNS TTLs
- add quick fallback in routing policy to prefer AZ with >=75% ready endpoints

marta: running resync now: `kubectl annotate svc infer-gpu redwood/force-slice-resync=true --overwrite`
infra-bot: endpointslice-controller: resync requested for service infer-gpu by marta
kevin: clearing conntrack on lb-egress-azb (one-liner):
```bash
ssh lb-egress-azb -- sudo conntrack -D -d 10.2.5.8 --proto tcp || true
```
marta: did resync + conntrack clear, monitoring :eyes:
alyssa: adding a temporary routing rule in edge-router to deprioritize AZ-b for 2m while we stabilize
sara: after actions, error rate dropped to baseline in ~45s. no more 502s from synthetic healthchecks
kevin: we should add a playbook entry: when spot drain + ipvs -> force slice resync + conntrack clear + routing deprioritize AZ. saves debugging time
marta: filed infra ticket INF-3421 with steps + links to logs :thumbsup:
kevin: nice. follow-up: look into kube-proxy conntrack GC tuning and endpoint slice controller backoff for large clusters
marta: great catch team :tada:
